bank.q: I ___ in this city since 2019.
bank.why: Since + titik waktu di masa lalu, masih berlanjut: present perfect (have lived).

bank.q: She ___ her keys, so she can't get in.
bank.why: Kejadian lampau dengan akibat sekarang (tidak bisa masuk): present perfect.

bank.q: My brother ___ a doctor.
bank.why: Subjek tunggal orang ketiga (my brother) memakai is.

bank.q: We ___ students at this school.
I ___ very tired today.
___ your parents at home?
She ___ coffee every morning.
bank.why: Subjek she (orang ketiga tunggal) menambah -s pada kata kerja.

bank.q: They ___ to school by bus.
He ___ not like fish.
bank.why: Negatif orang ketiga tunggal: does not + kata kerja dasar.

bank.q: ___ you speak English?
My mother ___ at a bank.
I have ___ apple in my bag.
bank.why: Apple diawali bunyi vokal, jadi an.

bank.q: She is ___ teacher.
bank.why: Teacher diawali bunyi konsonan, jadi a.

bank.q: He waits for ___ hour.
There are three ___ in the room.
bank.why: Jamak tak beraturan: child menjadi children.

bank.q: I see two ___ in the garden.
She has five ___.
The book is ___ the table.
The cat is ___ the box.
bank.why: In untuk berada di dalam sesuatu.

bank.q: The class starts ___ 8 o'clock.
My birthday is ___ June.
We have a meeting ___ Monday.
This is Anna. ___ is my friend.
Give the book to ___.
bank.why: Setelah to dipakai bentuk objek: me.

bank.q: This is not your bag. It is ___.
bank.why: Mine berdiri sendiri tanpa kata benda (milikku).

bank.q: That is ___ car. (milik Tom)
Your mother's sister is your ___.
You drink ___ with a straw.
bank.why: Juice (jus) diminum; rice dan bread dimakan.

bank.q: I ___ up at six every day.
___ is your name?
bank.why: Menanyakan nama: What is your name?

bank.q: ___ do you live?
___ old are you?
There ___ two pens on the desk.
She ___ swim very well.
bank.why: Can tidak berubah dan langsung diikuti kata kerja dasar.

bank.q: ___ the door, please.
bank.why: Kalimat perintah memakai kata kerja dasar.

bank.q: Look! It ___ now.
bank.why: Kejadian yang sedang berlangsung: is + V-ing.

bank.q: I ___ a book at the moment.
bank.why: At the moment menandakan sedang terjadi: am reading.

bank.q: Yesterday I ___ to the market.
She ___ a cake last night.
They ___ not come to the party.
bank.why: Negatif lampau: did not + kata kerja dasar.

bank.q: The number 13 is ___.
I ___ never ___ sushi.
bank.why: Pengalaman sampai sekarang: have + past participle (eaten).

bank.q: She ___ here for ten years.
bank.why: For + lama waktu, masih berlanjut: present perfect.

bank.q: Have you ___ your homework yet?
I ___ him last week.
bank.why: Waktu lampau jelas (last week): past simple.

bank.q: ___ you ever been to Bali?
bank.why: Ever + pengalaman hidup: Have you ever been.

bank.q: I ___ TV when the phone rang.
bank.why: Kegiatan berlangsung lalu terpotong: past continuous.

bank.q: While she ___, he was cooking.
bank.why: Dua kegiatan bersamaan di masa lalu.

bank.q: Look at those clouds. It ___ rain.
bank.why: Prediksi berdasarkan bukti sekarang: going to.

bank.q: The phone is ringing. I ___ answer it.
This bag is ___ than that one.
English is ___ than I thought.
This book is ___ than the first one.
She is the ___ student in the class.
It was the ___ movie I have ever seen.
You ___ wear a seat belt. It is the law.
You ___ smoke here. It is forbidden.
You ___ come early. We start late.
___ I borrow your pen?
bank.why: May I... = meminta izin dengan sopan.

bank.q: If it rains, we ___ at home.
bank.why: Conditional tipe 1: if + present, will + kata kerja.

bank.q: If I ___ rich, I would travel the world.
If you heat ice, it ___.
bank.why: Fakta ilmiah (tipe 0): present simple di kedua klausa.

bank.q: The window ___ by the boy yesterday.
English ___ all over the world.
There isn't ___ milk left.
How ___ eggs do you need?
I have ___ friends here, so I feel lonely.
bank.why: Few (tanpa a) = hampir tidak ada, bernada negatif.

bank.q: The man ___ lives next door is a pilot.
The book ___ I bought is great.
That is the girl ___ bag was stolen.
I enjoy ___ to music.
She decided ___ a new job.
He is good at ___ pictures.
Please ___ your shoes before you enter.
I'm ___ for my keys. Have you seen them?
The flight was ___ because of the storm.
She said that she ___ tired.
bank.why: Ucapan dilaporkan mundur satu tense: is menjadi was.

bank.q: You like tea, ___?
bank.why: Kalimat positif, tag negatif dengan auxiliary yang sama.

bank.q: Could you tell me where ___?
bank.why: Pertanyaan tidak langsung memakai urutan kalimat biasa.

bank.q: I have a job ___ tomorrow at ten.
Can you ___ me some money until Friday?
The ___ of this shirt is thirty dollars.
bank.why: Price = harga yang tertera pada barang.

bank.q: I ___ my keys. I can't find them anywhere.
You must show your ___ at the airport.
If I ___ harder, I would have passed.
bank.why: Tipe 3 (andai lampau): if + past perfect, would have + pp.

bank.q: She would have come if she ___ about it.
bank.why: Past perfect di klausa if untuk penyesalan masa lalu.

bank.q: I wish I ___ more free time.
bank.why: Wish tentang keadaan sekarang yang berlawanan: past simple.

bank.q: I wish I ___ that email yesterday.
bank.why: Penyesalan masa lalu: wish + past perfect.

bank.q: When I arrived, the film ___.
bank.why: Kejadian yang lebih dulu dari titik lampau: past perfect.

bank.q: I'm exhausted. I ___ all day.
bank.why: Kegiatan berlangsung terus sampai sekarang: present perfect continuous.

bank.q: The report ___ by Friday.
bank.why: Future perfect pasif: will have been + pp.

bank.q: He is said ___ three languages.
bank.why: It is said that he speaks = He is said to speak.

bank.q: Never ___ such a beautiful sunset.
bank.why: Kata negatif di awal membalik subjek dan auxiliary.

bank.q: Not only ___ late, but he also forgot the files.
If I had taken that job, I ___ in London now.
bank.why: Sebab lampau, akibat sekarang: would + V (bentuk sekarang).

bank.q: ___ the heavy rain, the match continued.
bank.why: Despite diikuti kata benda; although diikuti klausa.

bank.q: He was late ___ he missed the bus.
The plan was good; ___, it was too expensive.
I was tired, ___ I went to bed early.
It's raining cats and dogs. It means it's ___.
"Break a leg!" means ___.
bank.why: Ucapan semoga sukses, biasanya sebelum tampil.

bank.q: "To be under the weather" means to feel ___.
"Piece of cake" means something ___.
She ___ a decision after a long talk.
Please ___ attention to the instructions.
We need to ___ a break. We've been working for hours.
She is allergic ___ peanuts.
He is afraid ___ heights.
I'm interested ___ learning French.
We arrived ___ the airport at noon.
___ honesty is important in ___ life.
She plays ___ piano beautifully.
He asked me where I ___.
bank.why: Pertanyaan dilaporkan mundur tense dan memakai urutan biasa.

bank.q: She told me ___ late.
bank.why: Perintah dilaporkan: tell + objek + (not) to + kata kerja.

bank.q: Please ___ the form before Friday.
bank.why: Fill in a form = mengisi formulir.

bank.q: The company decided to ___ 50 new staff.
His speech was very ___; everyone was moved.
The weather will ___ my plans.
bank.why: Affect (kata kerja) = memengaruhi; effect = dampak (kata benda).

bank.q: She gave me good ___ about my career.
He ___ to know the answer, but he didn't.
I suggest that he ___ a doctor.
bank.why: Setelah suggest (that), dipakai bentuk dasar kata kerja.

bank.q: It is essential that she ___ on time.
bank.why: Subjunctive: bentuk dasar setelah kata sifat seperti essential.

bank.q: He ___ have left already; his coat is gone.
bank.why: Must have + pp = kesimpulan yakin tentang masa lalu.

bank.q: You ___ have told me earlier! Now it's too late.
bank.why: Should have + pp = kritik/penyesalan tentang masa lalu.

bank.q: She ___ be at home; I'm not sure.
Hardly ___ arrived when it started to rain.
bank.why: Hardly di awal: inversi dengan had.

bank.q: Only after the meeting ___ the truth.
___ I need is a good night's sleep.
It was Maria ___ solved the problem.
bank.why: Kalimat cleft: it was + orang + who.

bank.q: The new law is ___; nobody knows how to apply it.
Her ___ attitude made the team trust her.
The results were ___ with our earlier findings.
He tried to ___ the problem, but it only got worse.
bank.why: Alleviate = meringankan; aggravate = memperparah, tidak cocok dengan "tried to".

bank.q: The manager was ___ about the new budget; she hated it.
"To bite the bullet" means to ___.
bank.why: Menghadapi hal tidak enak dengan tabah.

bank.q: "The ball is in your court" means ___.
opts: it is your turn to decide

bank.q: "To cut corners" means to ___.
"Once in a blue moon" means ___.
The company ___ a huge profit last year.
We must ___ the risks before investing.
She ___ a good point during the debate.
___ the door, he found the room empty.
bank.why: Participle aktif: dia sendiri yang membuka, jadi opening.

bank.q: ___ in 1990, the bridge is still in use.
bank.why: Participle pasif: jembatan dibangun, jadi built.

bank.q: He works ___ a translator at a bank.
She sings ___ a professional.
I am used to ___ up early.
I ___ play football when I was a kid.
bank.why: Used to + kata kerja dasar = dulu biasa.

bank.q: I had my car ___ yesterday.
bank.why: Have + objek + past participle = menyuruh orang lain mengerjakan.

bank.q: She got her hair ___ at the salon.
___ you hurry, you will miss the train.
Tom is outgoing, ___ his brother is shy.
It was ___ a long film that I fell asleep.
bank.why: Such + a + kata sifat + kata benda.

bank.q: The film was ___ long that I fell asleep.
The soup is not hot ___ to drink.
It is ___ cold to swim today.
Which is the most formal request?
opts: Could you possibly send me the file?
bank.why: Could you possibly... sangat sopan dan formal.

bank.q: Which is the best reply to "How do you do?"
bank.why: How do you do? dijawab dengan pertanyaan yang sama (sapaan formal perkenalan).

bank.q: For a formal email, the best opening is ___.

articles.title: A Day at the Market
body: Every Sunday, Rina goes to the market with her mother. They leave home at six in the morning because the best vegetables are sold early.
First, they buy tomatoes, onions and chilies. Rina likes to choose the tomatoes herself. She looks for ones that are red and a little soft.
Then they buy fish and chicken. The seller knows her mother well, so he gives them a good price. After two hours, their bags are full and they take a motorbike taxi home.

qs.q: Why do they leave early?
opts: The best vegetables are sold early.
Rina is afraid of the traffic.

qs.q: What does Rina look for in a tomato?
opts: It is red and a little soft.

qs.q: How do they go home?

articles.title: My New Neighbor
body: Last week, a new family moved into the house next to ours. The father is a teacher and the mother is a nurse. They have a son named Dimas.
Dimas is twelve years old. He loves football, so my brother invited him to play after school. They played for an hour and became friends.
In the evening, my mother brought some cake to their house. The neighbors were very happy and said thank you. I think we will get along well.

qs.q: What is the father's job?
Who invited Dimas to play?
Why did the narrator's mother visit the neighbors?

articles.title: Why Sleep Matters
body: Many people think that sleeping less gives them more time to work. In fact, scientists have found that the opposite is often true. When we do not sleep enough, our brain works more slowly and we make more mistakes.

Adults usually need seven to nine hours of sleep each night. Teenagers need even more, because their bodies are still growing. Students who sleep well tend to remember lessons better than those who stay up late.

There are simple ways to sleep better. Go to bed at the same time every day, avoid phones for an hour before sleeping, and keep your room dark and quiet. After a week or two, most people notice that they feel more energetic during the day.

qs.q: What happens when we do not sleep enough?
Who needs more than seven to nine hours of sleep?
Which tip is NOT mentioned?
opts: Go to bed at the same time

articles.title: The Bicycle Commuter
body: Andi used to drive to work every day. The trip took an hour because of the traffic, and parking cost him a lot of money. One morning, he decided to try something different and rode his bicycle instead.

At first, it was difficult. He arrived tired and sweaty, and his legs hurt for days. However, after a month, he was surprised to find that the ride only took forty minutes, and he felt healthier than before.
Now Andi saves money on fuel and parking, and he has lost three kilos. He says the only problem is the rain. On rainy days, he still takes the bus, but he can't wait to get back on his bicycle.

qs.q: Why did Andi stop driving?
How long does the bicycle ride take?
What does Andi do on rainy days?

articles.title: Learning from Mistakes
body: When Sari started learning English, she was afraid of speaking. She worried that people would laugh at her pronunciation, so she stayed silent in class for months.

Her teacher noticed this and gave her a small task: say one sentence a day to a classmate. Sari did it, and although she made many errors, nobody laughed. Instead, her classmates corrected her kindly.
Today, Sari speaks with confidence. She says that every mistake taught her something new. "If I had never tried," she says, "I would still be silent."

qs.q: Why was Sari silent in class?
opts: She was afraid people would laugh.

qs.q: What was the teacher's task?
How did her classmates react?

articles.title: The Rise of Remote Work
body: Over the past few years, remote work has changed from an occasional perk into a normal way of working for millions of people. Technology made this possible, but it was the pandemic that forced companies to try it on a large scale.

The advantages are clear. Employees save the time and money they used to spend commuting, and many report better balance between work and family life. Companies, in turn, can hire talented people regardless of where they live.

Nevertheless, remote work is not perfect. Some workers feel isolated, and the line between work and rest can easily disappear. Managers also find it harder to build team spirit through a screen. As a result, many organizations now prefer a hybrid model, in which employees work from home on some days and from the office on others.

qs.q: What made remote work spread on a large scale?
Which is a disadvantage mentioned?
What is a hybrid model?
opts: Working at home some days and at the office others

articles.title: Plastic in the Ocean
body: Every year, millions of tons of plastic end up in the ocean. Bottles, bags and fishing nets float on the surface or sink to the bottom, where they can remain for hundreds of years.

Marine animals suffer the most. Turtles mistake plastic bags for jellyfish, and birds feed pieces of plastic to their chicks. Even tiny fragments, known as microplastics, have been found in fish that people eat.

Although the problem seems overwhelming, solutions exist. Many countries have banned single-use bags, and volunteers regularly clean up beaches. Experts agree, however, that the most effective step is to reduce the amount of plastic we produce in the first place.

qs.q: Why do turtles eat plastic bags?
opts: They think the bags are jellyfish.

qs.q: What are microplastics?
What do experts say is most effective?

articles.title: A Letter to My Future Self
body: Dear me, ten years from now,

I am writing this on a rainy evening while preparing for my final exams. I am tired, a little nervous, and unsure about what I want to do after graduating. I hope that by the time you read this, you have found work that you enjoy.

I promise to keep learning, even when it feels hard. If you are reading this, I hope you have kept in touch with your old friends and have taken good care of our parents. Please remember that success is not only about money; it is also about being kind, healthy and at peace with yourself.

qs.q: When was the letter written?
What does the writer hope for?
According to the writer, success is also about ___.

articles.title: The Economics of Attention
body: In the digital age, attention has become one of the most valuable resources. Platforms that offer their services for free are not charities; they earn money by keeping users on their screens for as long as possible, then selling that attention to advertisers.

To achieve this, designers rely on techniques borrowed from psychology. Endless scrolling, unpredictable rewards and constant notifications are all intended to make it difficult to stop. Critics argue that these methods exploit human weaknesses rather than serve genuine needs.

Whether individuals can resist such pressure remains debatable. Some advocate personal discipline, such as limiting screen time, whereas others insist that responsibility should lie with the companies themselves. What is certain is that a debate about how we spend our attention is also a debate about how we wish to live.

qs.q: How do free platforms make money?
opts: By selling users' attention to advertisers

qs.q: Critics say the design techniques ___.
What do some people think should be responsible?

articles.title: Why Languages Disappear
body: Linguists estimate that there are roughly seven thousand languages in the world, yet nearly half of them are endangered. On average, one language falls silent every few weeks, usually when the last fluent speaker passes away.

The causes are rarely violent. More often, a community gradually shifts to a dominant language because it offers better access to education, jobs and media. Parents, wishing the best for their children, stop passing on the language at home, and within two or three generations it vanishes.

The loss is more than linguistic. Each language carries unique knowledge about nature, history and humor that cannot be translated perfectly. Fortunately, some communities have successfully revived their languages through schools, songs and digital dictionaries, proving that decline is not inevitable.

qs.q: Why do most languages disappear?
opts: Communities shift to a dominant language

qs.q: What happens when parents stop speaking the language at home?
opts: It can vanish within a few generations

qs.q: What does the writer say about revival?
opts: It has worked in some communities.
